transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. We're here for the mandatory round-robin sign-off on the televised opening-night tribute broadcast operating plan before I can issue final approval. As we all know, the tribute is scheduled for 9:00 PM in the Grand Lyric Theater, and the draft plan calls for an eight-minute in-person full-band performance with a 90-second song excerpt, a confetti drop, and four stagehands. I need each of you — technical, rights, talent, and safety leads — to state your exact final operating requirement for your area and name one concrete update you will enter in the production records. Let's begin. Technical lead, you're up first.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During a broadcast line test this afternoon, I measured a 180-millisecond latency that makes a live instrumental feed unusable with the house video system. The tested workaround is a pre-recorded instrumental stem with live vocals. I have not entered this result in the sign-off packet yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue before we proceed. My written license confirmation, which I received today but have not yet updated in the rights tracker, permits only a 45-second excerpt of the tribute recording — not the 90 seconds called for in the draft plan. The license also forbids any replay after the broadcast and requires the on-screen credit 'Music courtesy of Meridian Songs.'
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical talent issue before we proceed. I confirmed with the lead performer's agent this morning that the lead can appear only remotely from 8:50 PM to 9:00 PM — not in person. The draft plan calls for an in-person full-band performance, but the lead performer cannot be there in person at all. This agent email is still awaiting entry on the talent calendar.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety issue before we proceed. The post-rehearsal safety inspection found that confetti is prohibited beneath the Grand Lyric Theater's sprinkler array, and a clear audience aisle measuring exactly 1.5 meters is required. I received these inspection minutes after the draft plan circulated and have not yet amended that draft. The draft plan's confetti drop directly violates the sprinkler-array prohibition, and no aisle clearance has been specified. My final operating requirement for safety is: no confetti drop may occur beneath the sprinkler array, and a clear audience aisle of exactly 1.5 meters must be maintained. The concrete update I will enter in the production records is the post-rehearsal safety inspection finding documenting the confetti prohibition and the 1.5-meter aisle requirement.
transcript.speaker: A5
